definitions.meaning: to keep a tally of points in a game is to mark them down
a surface that has been cut with lines or grooves has been marked this way

explanation.surface: Someone noted down that a disc or document was damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one verb: noting points in a game, and cutting lines into a surface.

clue.text: Yet a crooked dealer may deal himself one

definitions.text: Yet a crooked dealer may deal himself one

parts.words: Yet a crooked dealer may deal himself one
parts.note: a poker hand of five cards in sequence, ironically honest-sounding for a cheating card dealer

explanation.definitionFit: In poker a run of five consecutive cards has the name meaning honest, the opposite of crooked.

indicators.note: the letters are arranged more loosely, so they are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something encourages a person to talk with less restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more freely' rearranges ONE SPOUT; the whole clue also defines the phrasal verb, as loosening up makes someone speak freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To become more talkative and frank is to loosen up and expand on things.

clue.text: One may get one's hooks into them

definitions.text: One may get one's hooks into them

parts.words: One may get one's hooks into them
parts.note: the small loops on clothing that hooks fasten into, as in hook-and-eye fasteners

explanation.definitionFit: Dressmakers' fasteners pair a metal hook with a small loop it catches in.

indicators.note: the money is placed within the other word as a deposit goes into a bank

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a cent is a small coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone has deposited cash at the bank not long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun where money is deposited; here it is the verb, as in 'bank on', giving RELY, with CENT put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean not long ago, a straight synonym.

definitions.meaning: weighing up an idea, as in thinking about an offer
having guests round and hosting them

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both weighing up a proposal and hosting guests at home.

clue.text: Catch sight of a man who endangers western security?

definitions.text: a man who endangers western security?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., an eastern agent, a threat to the West

explanation.surface: Someone notices a dangerous foreign agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To glimpse something is to spot it; split as E plus an agent it is an Eastern operative.

definitions.meaning: leaned towards, as in ... to do something

explanation.surface: Someone is disposed to be cautious.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both leaning towards a habit and looking after something.

parts.note: not slight familiarity but a person who always nods agreement

explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who agrees with everything nods along to whatever is said.

definitions.meaning: a short double-breasted jacket worn outdoors, the sailor's coat of that name

explanation.surface: A damaged hinge or knuckle could be worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a rolled cannabis cigarette and a thick double-breasted outdoor jacket.

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it, the way posts might include an extra

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a tip is a gratuity left for service

explanation.surface: A list of job postings mentions a tip on top of the basic pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posts' looks like jobs, which fits 'wages'; here it is the verb, sending by mail, giving SENDS around TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipends are fixed regular payments, a form of salary or pay.

clue.text: Few still show coarse male expressions of admiration

indicators.note: something coarse is rough and crude, so these letters are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Only a handful of men still make crude noises to show they fancy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coarse' rearranges FEW STILL SHOW; it also fits the surface, as the answer is a crude habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-note whistle men direct at an attractive passer-by signals crude appreciation.

clue.text: Cut down this month, in a way

parts.note: taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street, a way or road

explanation.surface: A reduction is being made this month, in a certain manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' marks the definition as a shortened word: the old business-letter abbreviation for 'instant', meaning of the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: In formal correspondence the short form of instant was used to mean of the present month.

indicators.note: the clue tells us the word is heard rather than read, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: a horde is a large crowd or throng

explanation.surface: Someone is told to collect a group of people, or so it is rumoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather a crowd' reads as one phrase, but 'Gather' alone is the definition: to amass and store things away.
explanation.definitionFit: To stockpile is to gather and store up a secret supply.

clue.text: Our last letter to the Greeks

definitions.text: Our last letter to the Greeks

parts.words: Our last letter to the Greeks
parts.note: our alphabet ends in Z; the Greek letter with that sound is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's sixth letter corresponds to the English Z, the final letter of our alphabet.

clue.text: Soldier in rising sea gets shelter

indicators.note: the soldier goes in the other word, inside it
in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier caught in a heavy sea reaches safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SEA into AES, and 'in' puts GI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Under someone's aegis means under their protection, so the word is a kind of protective cover.

clue.text: Order cathead to be immersed in the rising tide

indicators.note: the letter is plunged inside the other word like something under water
in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
read as cat's head, the first letter of cat

explanation.surface: Someone instructs that a ship's cathead beam be submerged by the incoming tide.
explanation.walkthrough: A cathead is a beam on a ship's bow, but here it splits into cat's head, C. 'rising' turns TIDE into EDIT, and C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree, an authoritative command.

parts.note: a flimsy structure built from playing cards, read whimsically as a building given over to card games

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a precarious scheme likely to collapse, and literally a home of playing cards.

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to expire is to die
to abet is to help or assist

explanation.surface: Someone passes away untreated because of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'outside': DIES around ABET.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a chronic condition in which the body cannot regulate blood sugar, an illness.

clue.text: It was instrumental in combining rest and play

indicators.note: the letters are combined and mixed together into one new word

explanation.surface: Something played a key part in balancing relaxation and fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumental' looks like 'helpful', but the definition is literal: an old stringed instrument. 'combining' mixes REST and PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a medieval plucked stringed instrument, now obsolete, hence 'was'.

clue.text: Chap finds his badly cooked meal — a takeaway?

indicators.note: something cooked badly is messed up, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man discovers his dinner has been ruined in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly cooked' is the anagram signal on CHAP FINDS HIS; the definition is the classic British takeaway meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Battered fried cod or haddock with fried potato chips is Britain's traditional takeaway dinner.

clue.text: Critically reviews part of the bible

definitions.meaning: assesses or evaluates, as a critic does
a book of the Old Testament following Joshua

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means assesses, and the same word names an Old Testament book about Israel's early leaders.

clue.text: Worked on the farm, drew about ll

indicators.note: one word goes about the other, around it

parts.note: to draw a match is to tie it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer sketched around a couple of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drew' looks like sketching, but it means drawing a game, TIED, which goes about LL.
explanation.definitionFit: To till land is to plough and cultivate soil, farm work.

indicators.note: the word is found as a piece of the longer word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone mentions one round of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is one individual thing, a single item.

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American
taken as written
read as gate's head, the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: A US citizen in the northern English town of Gateshead finds work there.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England opposite Newcastle; split into gate's head it gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean putting something to work, a synonym.

indicators.note: the clue says the word sounds like another, so it is heard not read

parts.note: able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at third man appears quite capable.
explanation.walkthrough: Third man is a cricket fielding position, but here it is Adam and Eve's second son, the third man in Genesis after Adam and Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, after Adam and Cain, the next male born was Cain's murdered younger brother.

parts.note: to bar is to ban or prohibit

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned pub north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, which fits the surface, but it is the verb meaning prohibit. The definition is loose: a town in Scotland, a west-coast port.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a port town on Scotland's west coast, a ferry hub for the Hebrides.

parts.note: a sweet sticky palm fruit, and also an engagement to meet someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sweet, sticky palm fruit and a romantic engagement.

parts.note: something that can be hit with a club and is round all over, not a sociable versatile player

explanation.definitionFit: A small dimpled sphere is struck with clubs on a course and is round in every direction.

clue.text: The stock market is the place to buy them

definitions.text: The stock market is the place to buy them

parts.words: The stock market is the place to buy them
parts.note: livestock sold at a farm market, not shares traded on an exchange

explanation.definitionFit: Livestock such as cows are bought and sold at an agricultural market.

indicators.note: a dancer swirling around suggests the letters spinning into a new order

explanation.surface: A ballerina from Africa's Khartoum spins on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swirling' turns DANSEUSE into the answer; Khartoum is the capital of Sudan, so 'perhaps' marks the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Khartoum is the capital of the African country, so someone from there is a native of it.

definitions.meaning: a cow that lows, the breed of Channel Island dairy cattle
a knitted pullover worn on the top half of the body

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing for either the bottom or top half of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A Channel Island dairy breed of cow shares its name with a woollen pullover worn on the torso.
